quarterly_data.signal: Q2 and H1 results (management, earnings call): Q2 revenue NT$484 hundred million, up 26.8% YoY and a record for the period; gross margin 23.1%, up 4.7 points YoY and also a record; operating profit NT$37.6 hundred million (up NT$13.4 hundred million YoY); net profit NT$37.3 hundred million, up 168.6% YoY. H1 revenue NT$891.6 hundred million, up 13.9% YoY (record); H1 gross margin 22.4% and operating margin 6.5% (up 5.9 and 3.4 points); H1 EPS NT$3.55 vs NT$1.3 a year ago. Server + optical-module + IC-substrate combined revenue grew 113% YoY to NT$192.7 hundred million, lifting their share of revenue from 11.7% to 21.6%. Net cash NT$261.5 hundred million; debt ratio down to 39.7% from 45%. Management estimates 70% to 80% of revenue is AI-related. H1 R&D spend rose NT$26.1 hundred million YoY on new-product sampling for plants not yet built.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue NT$484 hundred million (+26.8% YoY), gross margin 23.1% (+4.7pp); net profit NT$37.3 hundred million (+168.6%); H1 revenue NT$891.6 hundred million (+13.9%), EPS NT$3.55; server/optical/substrate revenue +113% YoY to 21.6% of total

quarterly_data.signal: 1.6T optical-module PCB: current orders are mainly 1.6T high-speed optical-module boards; 2026 optical-module related revenue is guided to double, 1.6T keeps growing sharply in 2027 and becomes the main shipping spec in 2028, and 3.2T boards are already being sampled. Customers are already pre-booking 2027 capacity; target is to become the world's largest high-end optical-module PCB supplier in 2027. 800G-and-above optical-module boards require M7-class ultra-low-loss laminate (1.6T effectively mandates it); management says roughly 20 players claim to be entering optical modules but few master M7 high-layer board production, which is why Zhen Ding's substrate-derived M7 technology gave it the 1.6T breakout. 1.6T optical-module board yield is described as industry-leading at above 90%, including the newly ramped Thailand lines. On a potential US FCC ban on Chinese optical modules: Zhen Ding supplies the PCB inside the module, not the module itself, so sees no direct hit, and can shift production to Thailand where customers require it. On CPO: the company says it will participate in both pluggable and CPO/NPO architectures as they develop; most PCB equipment is transferable between product types so a CPO shift would strand little capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 optical-module revenue to double; 1.6T main spec by 2028; 3.2T sampling; 1.6T board yield above 90%; goal: largest high-end optical-module PCB supplier in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Materials supply: T-glass is currently in shortage; Zhen Ding says it keeps long-term strategic partnerships with upstream material makers, has signed strategic-cooperation / supply-guarantee agreements with suppliers, and is qualifying second sources to diversify. Whether next-generation glass-core substrates relieve the glass supply-demand balance is 'not yet knowable' given long certification. CCL price increases are being passed through to customers smoothly with small impact on gross margin; across AI and non-AI products management says most raw-material increases can be passed on.

Capacity and outlook: 2026 capex is around NT$800 hundred million, with similarly high investment maintained for 2027-2028; 13 plants are under construction and 16 more planned. Capex split roughly: 25% to 30% optical-module boards, 35% to 40% IC substrate (substrate is the most capital-intensive - a dollar of high-end substrate investment yields only about half a dollar of output, versus six to seven tenths for server/optical boards). Thailand: PA01 reached breakeven and turned profitable in July 2026 (mass production began Q3 2025); additional Thai buildings and a data/computing center complete around end-2026; Thai plants 1-2 make server and optical-module boards, plant 3 flex, plant 4 high-layer-count server boards. Huai'an HD campus broke ground 04-22-2026, three buildings already topped out, production starts March 2027 with fast ramp since qualification is shared with the existing campus. Shenzhen third campus broke ground 07-24-2026 for AI 1.6T optical-module high-layer boards and high-end AI flex; its supplier conference drew 217 supply-chain companies and 410 representatives. Capacity for the next three years is largely bound to customers through LTAs and project-based binding agreements (visibility to 2029); 2027 AI PCB order visibility described as optimistic with capacity still insufficient. By 2030 the target is server + optical-module + IC-substrate at 45% to 50% of group revenue. GPU customer motherboards are produced both in mainland China and Thailand depending on customer requirements. Subsidiary Peng Ding filed its Hong Kong main-board listing application on July 2, 2026 (under review, so details withheld).
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex ~NT$800 hundred million; 13 plants building + 16 planned; capex split 25-30% optical module / 35-40% IC substrate; Thailand PA01 profitable July 2026; 2030 target 45-50% of revenue from server/optical/substrate
